visible.title: Running Streamlit with Starlette in Corporate Network
visible.body:
### Checklist

### Summary

I have a Streamlit application with multiple subpages that I run within a corporate network. Due to the new functionalities, I would like to upgrade to Streamlit >= 1.57. However, I am encountering difficulties getting a minimal example to run, even though it works without issues on my private machine.

app.py:
```python
import streamlit as st
app = st.App("test_page.py")
``` 

test_page.py:

```python
import streamlit as st
st.header("Welcome")
st.write("This is the main page of the app.")
``` 

When I start app.py using streamlit run app.py, I can access the page at http://127.0.0.1:8501/, but I cannot see it at http://localhost:8501/. Instead I just see the loading screen:

[image]

When running on the server, I am facing similar issues. I expect that when I am able to run the application on localhost, it should be possible in the same way on the server.

In the Dev-Tools of the browser I see this message:
_index.dkY5s53S.js:184 WebSocket connection to 'ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream' failed: WebSocket is closed before the connection is established._

In the Terminal I get the following error message: 
_Exception in callback _ProactorBasePipeTransport._call_connection_lost(None)
handle: <Handle _ProactorBasePipeTransport._call_connection_lost(None)>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\Users\<user>\.conda\envs\scnd_1_58\Lib\asyncio\events.py", line 88, in _run
    self._context.run(self._callback, *self._args)
  File "C:\Users\<user>\.conda\envs\scnd_1_58\Lib\asyncio\proactor_events.py", line 165, in _call_connection_lost
    self._sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054] An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host
Exception in callback _ProactorBasePipeTransport._call_connection_lost(None)
handle: <Handle _ProactorBasePipeTransport._call_connection_lost(None)>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\Users\<user>\.conda\envs\scnd_1_58\Lib\asyncio\events.py", line 88, in _run
    self._context.run(self._callback, *self._args)
  File "C:\Users\<user>\.conda\envs\scnd_1_58\Lib\asyncio\proactor_events.py", line 165, in _call_connection_lost
    self._sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054] An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host_

I would really happy to use the new version as it brings so much benefit for my use case. Unfortunately I tried various options for starting the application and all of them failed.

gold.summary: In a corporate network, Streamlit >=1.57 (Starlette) app doesn't load; works on private machine.
hypotheses: proxy/auth in corporate network breaking websocket under new server

missing_info.item: localhost resolution/binding and proxy bypass settings
missing_info.why: Separates IPv4/IPv6 or corporate interception from a server regression.

missing_info.item: Same minimal example on pre-Starlette version in the same network

acceptable_next_steps: Compare localhost versus 127.0.0.1, binding and proxy-bypass behavior with the supplied minimal app.
Compare the earlier version in the same environment and escalate reproducible differences with the existing console error.
must_not: Ask for the same browser console WebSocket error already pasted.
Claim later authentication/cookie analysis is initial knowledge.
Declare a confirmed Streamlit regression solely from private-versus-corporate behavior.
gold.reference: Confirmed regression; open; later linked to authentication.
gold.review_reason: The same machine works at 127.0.0.1 but not localhost, with explicit WebSocket failure already supplied. A targeted IPv4/IPv6, proxy-bypass and pre-Starlette comparison is more discriminating than immediately confirming a library regression. Escalation with the minimal example remains reasonable.

missing_info.item: does 1.56 (pre-Starlette) work in the same network

acceptable_next_steps: Ask for console errors and 1.56 comparison; escalate as regression with evidence

gold.acceptable_why: Hani: escalation with the minimal example remains reasonable
